newsitem.title: FRANCE: Agnelli holding raises stake in Club Med.
newsitem.headline: Agnelli holding raises stake in Club Med.

text.p: Italy's Agnelli group said on Tuesday it had raised its stake in French resort company Club Mediterranee to 19 percent from 13 percent.
A spokesman for Exor SA, a holding company controlled by members of the Agnelli family, told Reuters, "I can confirm that Exor holds 19 percent of Club Med".
He declined to say whether Exor might increase its stake.
Club Med, which operates vacation villages around the world, declined to comment.
Exor's move to raise its stake through share purchases in the open market strengthens its position as Club Med's leading shareholder.
It played an active role in bringing in former Euro Disney chairman Philippe Bourguignon to run Club Med in February.

Leading investors in the firm had paved the way for changes in its ownership structure last December by ending a shareholder pact. The six-year-old agreement had limited stakes among six big shareholders to 13 percent each.
Club Med announced Bourguignon's appointment in February after reporting a loss of 743 million francs ($128.7 million) for the year to October 31, including 820 million in restructuring charges.

Analysts said Exor, which had raised its stake a year before to 12.9 percent, led the charge against previous head Serge Trigano, son of the group's founder. Trigano was bumped up to head the supervisory board.
Shares in Club Med edged up 0.22 percent to 446 francs. Traders said investors viewd Exor as an active long-term investor and did not believe its move presaged a buyout bid. ($ = 5.772 French Francs)
